05.selection_reason: This variant contains application workspaces, a production multi-stage Dockerfile, compose, env template and operational scripts. The 05a sibling is documentation/toolkit only and has no package manifest, Dockerfile or compose file.

compose.tls_constraint: The edge proxy is loopback HTTP; public TLS must be supplied by an external proxy or by an explicitly adapted Caddy configuration.

production_images.runtime_media_tools: The common worker image installs ffmpeg, ffprobe, Python, OpenCV and NumPy; web excludes those tools.
production_images.reproducibility_gap: The Dockerfile installs unpinned Alpine ffmpeg packages and comments say ffmpeg 7 while project docs claim ffmpeg 8.1; confirm the actual built image version before deployment.

05.external_persistent_store: Cloud.ru-compatible S3 object storage is required for source and output media; production does not use the test MinIO service.

resource_basis.classification: component-based planning floor, not a measured production claim
cpu_ram_reasons: worker-stt runs up to two jobs concurrently and performs local ffmpeg extraction/chunking before remote STT
worker-video runs one ffmpeg render at a time and invokes Python/OpenCV face detection
web, PostgreSQL, Redis and three Node worker processes run concurrently
compose has no CPU or memory limits, so an oversized or adversarial media job can pressure the whole VM
disk_reasons: uploads are accepted up to 2,000,000,000 bytes
each source-processing worker reserves three times source bytes before download
STT concurrency two can reserve about 12 GB in stt-work; render concurrency one can reserve about 6 GB in render-work
the floor also leaves room for images, PostgreSQL, Redis AOF and Docker layers
resource_basis.browser_and_oom: Playwright browsers are test tooling launched by scripts/check-responsive.sh and are not part of production compose. Production OOM exposure is instead ffmpeg/OpenCV plus Node concurrency; face detection streams one raw frame at a time, but no container memory limit is present. Keep browser checks on a separate runner or budget extra RAM temporarily.

blockers: Provide an external env with all required ceilings, database/Redis/session secrets, public origin, S3 and OpenRouter configuration without copying repository secrets.
Choose and configure the public TLS ingress; the current edge profile binds only to loopback HTTP.
Confirm actual ffmpeg/ffprobe/OpenCV versions from the built worker image and set operational memory limits after a media smoke measurement.
Define backups for pgdata and model-spend; decide whether in-flight Redis/work volumes need crash-consistent recovery or can be reconstructed from PostgreSQL/S3.

compose.stand_dependency: compose.stand.yml requires the pre-existing external Docker network talk-ai-public and a separate shared TLS proxy.

production_images.proxy_note: Builds Caddy with the caddy-ratelimit module; production worker has no browser.

compose.public_behavior: The overlay removes the web host port, exposes only Caddy 80/443, and keeps PostgreSQL/assets private.

production_images.image: one application image used by web, worker and migrate

runnable_operations: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f compose.public.yml up -d web worker proxy

readiness_requirements: private asset directory is a real readable/writable/searchable directory
at least 512 MiB free on asset filesystem
health.worker_check: heartbeat JSON state ready and no older than 60 seconds

persistent_data.purpose: PostgreSQL source of truth and asset metadata
private user uploads, normalized images, self-contained GLB and share derivatives; mounted only by web/worker
Caddy certificate/state data in public overlay
Caddy config state in public overlay

asset_constraints: GLB upload maximum 25 MiB; reference/room image upload maximum 10 MiB
64 assets/project, 200 MiB/project and 1 GiB/account are the implemented storage ceilings
GLB validation allows up to 750,000 vertices, 250,000 triangles and two 8K-equivalent texture pixel budgets
local asset volume prevents naive independent web/worker replicas without a shared filesystem
backup_constraints: Architecture explicitly requires a consistent backup of PostgreSQL plus the assets volume because database rows contain private object keys, sizes and hashes.

For a restorable snapshot, quiesce web and worker writes, capture pg_dump or a database-consistent snapshot and the assets volume as one recovery point, then verify referenced files/hashes after restore.
Do not use docker compose down -v. Preserve tls-data/tls-config when moving the current endpoint or accept certificate reissuance as a separate edge operation.
Uncertain AI jobs and payment events must not be blindly replayed after restore; reconcile durable job/payment state.

resource_basis.classification: component-based planning floor, not a measured production claim
reasons: compose caps db, web and worker at 512 MiB each and proxy at 256 MiB, totaling 1.75 GiB before Docker and host overhead
sharp, tesseract and bounded GLB/image parsing can use native memory inside web/worker caps
40 GB is only an initial floor; retained private assets can grow to 1 GiB per account and database/TLS/Docker storage is additional
